comparisons.peer_topic: Competitive Landscape in Data Center Segment
comparisons.peer_summary: AMD competes in the Data Center segment primarily against Intel and NVIDIA with CPU, GPU, and DPU products, while also facing competition from Intel in FPGA and Adaptive SoC products. The competitive environment includes smaller fabless companies offering proprietary accelerators and Arm-based CPUs, as well as customers potentially developing internal microprocessor and accelerator products.
comparisons.comparison: Both disclosures detail AMD's competitive positioning and revenue drivers within the data center segment, which is a primary market for MU's CNBU products. MU reports that its CNBU sales in the data center market consist primarily of HBM and various DDR/LPDDR/GDDR DRAM products, driven by high-performance computing needs. AMD explicitly identifies NVIDIA and Intel as its primary competitors in the Data Center segment using CPU, GPU, and DPU server products, while also facing competition from smaller fabless companies offering proprietary accelerators. While MU discloses the specific product types (HBM/DDR) fueling its data center revenue, AMD discloses the competitive landscape (NVIDIA/Intel) and product classes (CPU/GPU/DPU) defining its data center business model.

sentences.text: CNBU sales to the data center, PC, and graphics markets in 2024 consisted primarily of our HBM, DDR5 and DDR4, LPDDR5, and GDDR6 DRAM products.
In the Data Center segment, we compete primarily against Intel Corporation (Intel) and NVIDIA Corporation (NVIDIA) with our CPU, GPU and DPU server products.
A variety of smaller fabless silicon companies offer proprietary accelerator solutions and Arm based CPUs targeting data center use-cases.
